claims.text: The target material is an as-deposited, non-equiatomic FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloy film approximately 100–200 nm thick.
The baseline film is deposited on a standard substrate without an engineered underlayer.
The controlled intervention is deposition of a 50–100 nm Cu underlayer immediately before HEA-film deposition.
Cu is a high-thermal-conductivity underlayer material.
Adding the Cu underlayer will enhance thermal coupling between the HEA film and substrate.
The Cu underlayer will increase the overall thermal conductivity of the multilayer system.
Improved multilayer thermal conductivity will increase the rate of heat exchange during magnetocaloric cycling.
Faster heat extraction will reduce the lag between magnetic-field changes and the film's thermal response.
Reducing thermal lag will reduce hysteresis losses during low-field magnetocaloric cycles.
The Cu-underlayer sample will have lower hysteresis than the otherwise equivalent sample without an underlayer.
The Cu underlayer will produce a sharper magnetocaloric peak.
Improved heat exchange will stabilize the magnetocaloric peak nearer the intrinsic phase-transition temperature.
The Cu-underlayer film's magnetocaloric response will more closely resemble bulk behavior than that of the baseline film.
The proposed operating field range is 0.1–0.3 T.
The proposed operating-temperature range is approximately 290–310 K.
The proposed mechanism is applicable only within the stated nanoscale layering and thermal-cycling conditions.
Underlayer uniformity and interface quality may affect the magnitude of the performance enhancement.
